note: Effort hours are estimates. Tasks marked guideline in their why line are Omega Games advice, not platform rules.

tasks.title: Write your one-sentence hook
tasks.why: Everything you post, pitch and put on a store page grows from this line.

tasks.title: Describe the player you are making this for
tasks.why: Picking one clear player makes every later choice easier: channels, tags, creators.

tasks.title: List five comparable games and what players praise in them
tasks.why: Comparable games tell you your tags, your price range and which creators to approach.

tasks.title: Draft your tag list from your comparable games
tasks.why: Tags decide where a store shows your game.

tasks.title: Pick your home base link
tasks.why: One link that every post points to keeps interest in one place you can measure.

tasks.title: Choose your main one or two channels
tasks.why: Fewer channels done steadily beat many done rarely (guideline).

tasks.title: Set a marketing budget cap, even if it is zero
tasks.why: A cap keeps tests small and honest. I never spend; this is for your planning.

tasks.title: Set up Steamworks and pay the Steam Direct fee
tasks.why: You need an app before a store page or keys. The fee is $100 per app and is recouped after $1,000 adjusted gross revenue.

tasks.title: Create your Epic Developer Portal organization
tasks.why: Epic onboarding includes verification that can take up to two weeks.

tasks.title: Create your itch.io page as a draft
tasks.why: A draft page lets you shape the page before anyone sees it.

tasks.title: Apply to each console program you want
tasks.why: Console programs review applications first, so start early. Terms are shared under NDA.

tasks.title: Set up your Apple and Google developer accounts
tasks.why: Store accounts and new-account testing steps come before any pre-order or pre-registration.

tasks.title: Search stores and socials for your game name
tasks.why: A clear, searchable name saves a rename later.

tasks.title: Start a simple numbers log (I keep it on your dashboard)
tasks.why: Your own numbers, week by week, are the only benchmark that matters here.

tasks.title: Confirm the art direction and core loop are settled before revealing
tasks.why: Players who follow early can be confused if the game changes a lot.

tasks.title: Make capsule art to spec, with a readable title
tasks.why: Capsules are the first thing players see; the title must be readable.

tasks.title: Capture at least 5 gameplay screenshots (1920x1080 or larger)
tasks.why: Screenshots must show gameplay only, no concept art or marketing text.

tasks.title: Capture a set of clean gameplay screenshots
tasks.why: Every store and press kit needs them.

tasks.title: Write the short description
tasks.why: A few hundred characters, plain text, no dates or "now available".

tasks.title: Write the "About this game" section
tasks.why: Show the core loop and what makes it different, with screenshots or GIFs.

tasks.title: Enter your tags in Steamworks, top 5 first
tasks.why: The top 5 tags carry the most weight.

tasks.title: Cut a short gameplay trailer
tasks.why: The first video on your page also becomes the short looping preview Steam shows in lists.

tasks.title: Run a store page review with me before submitting
tasks.why: A second look catches missing items before Steam review does.

tasks.title: Submit the store page for review in Steamworks (you press the button)
tasks.why: Steam asks for 7 business days before you want it live.

tasks.title: Publish as Coming Soon (you press the button)
tasks.why: Wishlists and your Community Hub start now.

tasks.title: Choose how the release date shows on Steam
tasks.why: Exact day, month, quarter, year or Coming Soon; lists sort by the last day of the range.

tasks.title: Publish your Epic product page for early awareness
tasks.why: Epic recommends publishing it at your announcement.

tasks.title: Make your itch.io page public or public restricted
tasks.why: Public restricted lets people follow before anything is for sale.

tasks.title: Put up a one-page website
tasks.why: A page you own, with the trailer, home base link and press kit link.

tasks.title: Build press kit version 1
tasks.why: When someone asks for details, you send one link.

tasks.title: Make one tracking link per channel
tasks.why: Steam reports wishlists and purchases per tracking link for signed-in visitors.

tasks.title: Draft your reveal announcement for each channel
tasks.why: A reveal is a good moment to ask for the first wishlists or follows.

tasks.title: Tidy your channel profiles with the home base link
tasks.why: Every profile should point to the same place.

tasks.title: Post a welcome note in your Steam Community Hub
tasks.why: The hub opens with your Coming Soon page.

tasks.title: Decide which languages you will support at launch
tasks.why: Store text and screenshots can be localized; pick only what you can support.

tasks.title: Start an email list sign-up on your website
tasks.why: You own this list. Commercial emails need a postal address and an easy opt-out in the US.

tasks.title: Prepare store listing art and preview video for mobile
tasks.why: Each store has its own listing assets.

tasks.title: Set a posting rhythm you can keep for months
tasks.why: Steady and small beats bursts you cannot repeat (guideline).

tasks.title: Capture a bank of 10 short gameplay clips
tasks.why: A ready bank makes every content prompt fast.

tasks.title: Write a devlog post about one real decision
tasks.why: Honest behind the scenes posts give people a reason to follow.

tasks.title: Run a playtest
tasks.why: Steam Playtest is a separate app, so it does not touch reviews or wishlists. itch.io works too.

tasks.title: Turn playtest feedback into a short change list
tasks.why: Players notice when you act on what they said.

tasks.title: Open a community space, if you can tend it weekly
tasks.why: An empty space hurts more than none (guideline).

tasks.title: Build a list of 30 creators who play games like yours
tasks.why: Personal outreach to the right people beats mass outreach (guideline).

tasks.title: Build a list of 15 outlets and writers who cover your genre
tasks.why: Look at who covered your comparable games.

tasks.title: Shortlist Steam Curators that cover your tags
tasks.why: Curator Connect sends review copies inside Steam with a personal note.

tasks.title: Check upcoming Steam themed events that match your game
tasks.why: Unreleased games and demos can appear in themed events that fit the theme.

tasks.title: Look at itch.io jams that fit a small side project
tasks.why: A jam game can be a low-cost way to meet players (guideline).

tasks.title: Plan a small paid test with a hard cap
tasks.why: Test one channel with one tracking link; you buy, I draft the ad copy and track your numbers.

tasks.title: Review the paid test with your own numbers
tasks.why: Keep, change or stop based on what you entered.

tasks.title: Post a monthly progress update on your store page
tasks.why: Store announcements keep the page alive for followers.

tasks.title: First keep-or-cut review of your channels
tasks.why: After four entries per channel, compare channels using your own numbers.

tasks.title: Refresh the press kit with new screenshots and trailer
tasks.why: Old assets make a game look older than it is.

tasks.title: Draft your Early Access answers
tasks.why: Be clear about what exists now and what is planned.

tasks.title: Make sure a gameplay trailer is up for Early Access
tasks.why: Steam asks for at least a gameplay trailer for Early Access.

tasks.title: Finish Google Play testing requirements if they apply to you
tasks.why: New personal accounts must meet them before pre-registration or production.

tasks.title: Decide whether to open App Store pre-orders
tasks.why: Pre-orders let people order early and the app downloads at release.

tasks.title: Decide whether to run Google Play pre-registration
tasks.why: Pre-registered players get a notice at launch.

tasks.title: Enter your console dates as you get them
tasks.why: I plan around your platform dates; I do not guess them.

tasks.title: Register for your chosen Next Fest (from the base game)
tasks.why: Registration is done on the base game, not the demo.

tasks.title: Have a public trailer on your store page before the registration deadline
tasks.why: Needed to be considered for the official festival trailer.

tasks.title: Set up the demo app in Steamworks
tasks.why: A demo is its own app tied to your base game.

tasks.title: Submit demo build and store items for review
tasks.why: Edition deadlines are firm; leave time to fix and resubmit.

tasks.title: Decide whether your demo is live for Press Preview
tasks.why: Releasing it makes it public for everyone, not only press.

tasks.title: Do your own QA pass on the demo
tasks.why: Build review checks it runs, not that it is bug free.

tasks.title: Set the demo live before the festival starts (you press the button)
tasks.why: Give yourself time to check it works.

tasks.title: Decide on festival livestreams (optional)
tasks.why: Optional. If you stream, test it before the festival.

tasks.title: Draft festival posts for each day
tasks.why: Tell people where to play and what to look for.

tasks.title: Send your live demo to creators on your list (you send)
tasks.why: Once the demo is public, a link is an easy yes for a creator, and no keys are needed.

tasks.title: Write down what you learned from the festival
tasks.why: Your own before and after numbers guide the final approach.

tasks.title: Decide how long the demo stays up after the festival
tasks.why: Players dislike demos that vanish without warning; tell them your plan.

tasks.title: Release your demo (you press the button)
tasks.why: A demo lets people try before they wishlist or buy.

tasks.title: Send the one-time demo notice to wishlisters (you press it)
tasks.why: Once per game, within two weeks of the demo release.

tasks.title: Draft demo launch posts
tasks.why: Point people to the demo and the home base link.

tasks.title: Final store page pass with me
tasks.why: Only show what will be in the launch build.

tasks.title: Check tags: at least 5, ideally up to 20
tasks.why: Required before launch.

tasks.title: Submit the launch build for review (recommended date)
tasks.why: Leaves room to fix and resubmit before the 7 business day minimum.

tasks.title: Confirm the release date before it locks
tasks.why: After the lock you cannot move the Steam date.

tasks.title: Set your price
tasks.why: Pricing permission is needed for release in Steamworks.

tasks.title: Decide on a launch discount
tasks.why: Steam allows 7 to 14 days, at most 40%, set before release.

tasks.title: Request creator and press keys
tasks.why: Pre-release keys are for small betas and press or creator access, never for sale.

tasks.title: Send review copies with Curator Connect (you send)
tasks.why: A personal note to curators who cover your tags.

tasks.title: Personal emails to creators on your list (you send)
tasks.why: One email per person, written for them.

tasks.title: Pitch emails to writers and outlets (you send)
tasks.why: Send early enough for them to plan coverage.

tasks.title: Follow-up drafts for anyone who has not replied (you send)
tasks.why: One polite follow-up, then let it go.

tasks.title: Finish the launch trailer
tasks.why: Put the newest trailer first on your page.

tasks.title: Build the launch-day run sheet with me
tasks.why: Who does what, hour by hour, on the day.

tasks.title: Draft launch announcements for every channel
tasks.why: Ready to copy and post when you press release.

tasks.title: Draft the launch email to your list (you send)
tasks.why: Your own list hears first.

tasks.title: Final press kit update with price, date and key art
tasks.why: Press needs the facts in one place.

tasks.title: Submit for Epic final review
tasks.why: Final review comes after onboarding and configuration.

tasks.title: Submit for App Review and Play review
tasks.why: Store review comes before release or pre-orders.

tasks.title: Prepare the itch.io release files and page
tasks.why: No review step, so test downloads yourself.

tasks.title: Plan your Early Access 1.0 date display
tasks.why: Steam lets Early Access games show a planned 1.0 date.

tasks.title: Set up a simple way for players to report bugs
tasks.why: Fast, visible fixes in week one matter (guideline).

tasks.title: Day before: check build, page, price, discount, run sheet
tasks.why: Catch surprises a day early.

tasks.title: Release (you press "Release App" or your store's button)
tasks.why: Nothing releases by itself.

tasks.title: Post your launch announcements (you post)
tasks.why: Same hour across your channels.

tasks.title: Post a launch announcement on your store page
tasks.why: Followers see store announcements.

tasks.title: Reply to comments and reviews for the first 48 hours
tasks.why: People notice a developer who answers.

tasks.title: Thank creators who covered the game (you send)
tasks.why: A short thank-you keeps the door open.

tasks.title: Ship and announce the first fix if needed
tasks.why: Clear patch notes build trust.

tasks.title: Enter launch week numbers
tasks.why: Your own launch numbers are your future benchmark.

tasks.title: Weekly review replies
tasks.why: Thank, answer, and note what to fix.

tasks.title: Plan and announce the first content or quality update
tasks.why: A visible update gives people a reason to come back.

tasks.title: Plan your first discount and seasonal sale
tasks.why: No regular discounts in the first 30 days; seasonal sales need 30 days since release.

tasks.title: Launch retrospective in your own numbers
tasks.why: What worked, what did not, what to keep.

tasks.title: Second round of creator outreach (you send)
tasks.why: Reach people who prefer released games.

tasks.title: Check Steam seasonal and themed events each month
tasks.why: Events are free visibility if your game fits.

tasks.title: Plan a gentle discount ladder
tasks.why: Steam suggests easing into discounts over time.

tasks.title: Pick an update cadence you can keep
tasks.why: Updates bring players back and can earn extra visibility.

tasks.title: Plan the 1.0 release as its own launch
tasks.why: Wishlisters are notified again at 1.0.

tasks.title: Write down what you would repeat for your next game
tasks.why: Your next launch starts with this one.

tasks.title: Consider adding languages based on where your players are
tasks.why: Steam shows regional wishlist and sales reports.
